name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, fully operative pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Defined by 47 O.S. §1-104 and regulated by 47 O.S. §11-1209.
restrictions: Two or three wheels, fully operative pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts
Class 1 and class 3 assist only while the rider is pedaling, stopping at 20 and 28 mph; class 2 can propel it without pedaling, up to 20 mph
The motor disengages when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be tampered with to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Riders under 16 may not operate a class 3, but may ride as a passenger on one designed to carry passengers
The rider has the rights and duties of a bicycle rider under the traffic laws, and may ride wherever bicycles are allowed
All three classes may ride bicycle and multiuse paths open to bicycles, unless the local authority or state agency in charge bans them
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the local authority or state agency in charge decides whether it's allowed
May not pass other vehicles between lanes of traffic
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, title or insurance
